Several recent papers address the issue of benchmark contamination and test-set leakage in Large Language Models (LLMs).

A notable paper in this area is **"TRUCE: Private Benchmarking to Prevent Contamination and Improve Comparative Evaluation of LLMs" [2403.00393]**. This paper highlights that the majority of current open-source benchmarks have been contaminated or leaked into LLMs, meaning the models have inadvertently had access to test data during their training phase, which compromises the validity of their performance evaluations.
